I've been farming this 50-mu plot for five years now, all in cabbage. My family depends on this income — four mouths to feed, and school fees coming up. I know what works here in Quzhou. The soil is decent, my well gives reliable water, and I've learned from neighbors and from my own mistakes.

I run three cabbage cycles a year on the same land. Spring is my most stable crop. Summer is hard — heat and pests hit heavy — but I can't leave the land idle, prices are decent if I hit the market window right. Autumn is my best season, the heads come out heavy and the price holds.

I use hybrid seeds because the yields justify the cost. I've tried traditional varieties and the size difference is obvious. I apply fertilizer in two or three splits — base dressing before planting, then topdress at heading. I keep irrigation consistent; cabbage suffers fast if it dries out, especially at heading.

Summer I spray more — aphids and Plutella are brutal in the heat. Spring and autumn are more manageable. I do rotary tillage between cycles to break up compaction and incorporate residue.

My 50 mu runs the same three cycles, so each crop gets the full plot.
